hypothesis: A 32-thread CTA with the existing factor-two target mapping preserves source reuse while testing a smaller launch configuration. The measured factor-two 64- and 128-thread configurations were similar (about 0.002617 s), while the 256-thread configuration was slower (about 0.002727 s); this does not establish how a 32-thread CTA will perform. Its scheduling and occupancy effects are hardware-dependent, and no speedup is assumed.
notes: This changes only the launch configuration: the existing two-target indexing, per-target bounds checks, exact masses, arithmetic, and zero shared-memory use remain unchanged. The controller should run the full correctness suite and official timing; register usage and occupancy were not independently measured here. Baseline timing was 0.0018473421 s, so prior coarsened candidates were slower in their recorded measurements.
transformations: Set the launch to 32 threads and 64 logical outputs per block to match the existing factor-two kernel indexing.
Keep shared_memory_bytes at zero and leave the kernel implementation unchanged.
